from_quote: I positively deny having any, the most distant desire of shutting the door of free discussion, on any subject which may benefit the people
rationale: Cato 2 (October 11, 1787) charged that Caesar "shuts the door of free deliberation and discussion"; in a paragraph addressed to Cato, Caesar states that charge and denies it.
to_quote: he shuts the door of free deliberation and discussion

from_quote: When I took notice of Cato's prefatory address to the Citizens of the State of New York, in your paper of the first instant
rationale: The paragraph refers to Caesar's own earlier piece "in your paper of the first instant", Caesar 1 (Daily Advertiser, October 1, 1787).

from_quote: I asserted, in my last, that the door of recommendation was shut, and cannot be opened by the same men — that the Convention was dissolved.
rationale: The paragraph repeats what Caesar "asserted, in my last": that the door of recommendation is shut and cannot be opened by the same men, and that the Convention is dissolved.
to_quote: the door of recommendation is shut and cannot be opened by the same men

from_quote: I cannot refrain from observing that Cato states very disingenuously the manner in which the Federal System came abroad
rationale: The paragraph restates Cato's account of how Congress received the Convention's plan (a power no authority could delegate, a government "founded on Jisnrpation" [OCR for usurpation], Congress "silent on its character") and sets out to dispute it.

from_quote: this consolidated system Congress did not approve and therefore have been silent on its character
rationale: The paragraph reproduces Cato's words that Congress "have been silent on its character" while naming Cato as their author.
to_quote: have been silent on its character

from_quote: the generous plan of power delivered down by their renowned for efatliers
rationale: The paragraph names Cato and turns back on him the words of his epigraph, "the generous plan of power deliver'd down by your renown'd Forefathers"; both passages are OCR-damaged ("pozver", "renozvn'd", "for efatliers").
to_quote: The generous plan of pozver deliver d down, "By your renozvn'd Forefathers

from_quote: Cato complains of my anticipating parts of his subject which he intended for future periods.
rationale: The paragraph names Cato and answers his complaint that Caesar "anticipated those observations" he meant to make later, which is in Cato 2 (October 11, 1787); this essay is dated October 15 and printed October 17.
